name: Optagelse.dk

coverage.includes: Every state-recognised undergraduate programme in Denmark — universities, university colleges, business academies and the artistic institutions.
coverage.excludes: Private providers outside the state system, and admission to individual subjects rather than a full programme.

choiceRules.note: You receive at most one offer: the highest-ranked programme that admits you. Lower choices are dropped automatically, so ranking a long shot first costs nothing. Rank by where you would rather be, not by how hard something is to get into.

identityRequirement: MitID. Sort this out in January — it is not something to discover on 14 March.
sharedSteps: Create the application in optagelse.dk using MitID and add up to eight programmes in priority order.
Upload documentation of anything you want counted, including work experience for quota 2.
Ask your IB coordinator to register you for the IB's results service so results reach the institutions directly.
Check whether any of your chosen institutions still requires a signature page — it is printed, signed by hand, and sent separately by post or email, never uploaded.
You can reorder priorities and add annexes until 12:00 on 5 July.
decisionModel: Programmes with more applicants than places split their intake into quota 1, allocated on the converted grade average alone, and quota 2, which weighs subject grades, up to twelve months of documented relevant work or study, and sometimes a test or essay. Applying by 15 March puts you in both automatically, provided your average can be converted to the Danish scale.
replyModel: Offers are published on 28 July together with every programme's quota 1 cut-off. You have a few days in early August to accept. Vacant places appear the same week.

notes: Aalborg is explicit that motivational letters and recommendations are not considered in its quota 2. Copenhagen Business School does want an essay. The rule is per institution.
